[[File:Oi Jinja Kasama Torii.jpg|250px|thumb|<center>Torii</center>]]
'''Ōi Shrine''' (おおいじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Kasama, Ibaraki|ja|笠間市}}, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|茨城県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} {{ill|theoretical shrine|ja|論社}} and was formerly ranked as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}.

== Deity ==
* '''{{ill|Kamiyai-mimi no Mikoto|ja|神八井耳命}}'''

=== About the enshrined deity ===
The enshrined deity, Kamiyai-mimi no Mikoto, was a son of the first {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}} and elder brother of the second {{ill|Emperor Suizei|ja|綏靖天皇}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, Kamiyai-mimi no Mikoto was the ancestor of the {{ill|Tomo clan|ja|多氏}} (descendants of Ōtomo). The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} records him as the ancestor of nineteen clans, including the Ōomi, the Oko-be no Muraji, Sakaai-be no Muraji, Hi no Kimi, Ōita no Kimi, Aso no Kimi, Chikushi Mikeno Muraji, Suzume no Omi, Suzume no Miyatsuko, Onagaya no Miyatsuko, Tsuge no Naori, Iyokuni no Miyatsuko, Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko, Michinoku Ishijō no Kuni no Miyatsuko, Jōdō Naka no Kuni no Miyatsuko, Nagasa no Kuni no Miyatsuko, Ise Funaki no Naori, Owari Niwa no Omi, and Shimada no Omi.

Among these, the area near this shrine is thought to have been governed by the {{ill|Nakakuni no Miyatsuko|ja|仲国造}} (Lord of Nakakuni), and it is believed that the shrine was established by the Nakakuni clan to worship their ancestor, Kamiyai-mimi no Mikoto.

== History ==
=== Foundation ===
According to shrine tradition, the shrine was built in {{ill|Daidō (Japan)|ja|大同}} 1 ({{ill|806|ja|806年}}) by imperial decree at Watai-ga-mine in Ōi Village, Naka District, Hitachi Province, and was called Ōi Daimyōjin.

=== Outline of history ===
In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, it is listed as “Ōi Shrine, Naka District, Hitachi Province,” included among the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}}. In the Middle Ages, it was called “Tarō Myōjin” and revered as the general guardian shrine of the five villages of Fukuda, Iida, Ishidera, Terasaki, and Hizawa. Among the four shrines of Ōi, Hakoda, Ishii, and Kurusu, this shrine was regarded as the foremost and worshiped as “Ichinomiya Myōjin” (Shisho Ichinomiya).

== Grounds ==
The main hall (honden) was rebuilt in {{ill|Meiwa|ja|明和}} 6 ({{ill|1769|ja|1769年}}). The sacred tree is a group of three cedar trees joined at the base, known as the “Parent and Child Cedars.”

<gallery>
File:Oi Jinja Kasama Honden.jpg|Main Hall (Honden)
File:Oi Jinja Kasama Oyakosugi.jpg|Parent and Child Cedars (Sacred tree)
</gallery>

== Festivals ==
* New Year’s Festival ({{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}})
* Spring Festival ({{ill|January 7|ja|1月7日}})
* Setsubun Festival ({{ill|February 3|ja|2月3日}})
* Rice-Planting Festival ({{ill|July 19|ja|7月19日}})
* Autumn Festival ({{ill|November 12|ja|11月12日}})
